description: Committee recommends early contracts for 60% of 2027-2028 water/sewer projects.
This aims to improve contractor availability and reduce costs.
It would limit future budget flexibility for these programs.

chips.text: Recommended
Staff explained early procurement could lead to cost savings and smoother construction.
Benefits contractors by allowing more time to plan and bid.
Committee recommends an exemption to policy for early procurement without approved budget.
Construction Association of Saskatchewan provided a letter regarding early procurement.
Administration will report back in 2028 on the pilot program's results.

description: Committee recommends extended noise bylaw hours for six 2026 events.
Events are at Prairieland, Brighton Core, Shakespeare, Kinsmen Park.

chips.text: Recommended
Nearby residents of condo buildings near Shakespeare on the Saskatchewan site.
Shakespeare on the Saskatchewan supported extensions for their two events.

speakers.name: Terresa Strohan
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Noise Bylaw Extension Requests
said: Supports noise bylaw extensions for Treehouse and Factor 8 events.
Event revenue is critical for charitable operations and site maintenance.
Strengthening event management, including communication with nearby residents.

description: Recommends applying for federal funding for 67 electric vehicles, 62 charging stations.
Project estimated to cost $1.7 million over three years.
Reduces 3,000 tons CO2 emissions over 10 years.

chips.text: Recommended
Taxpayers benefit from projected fuel and maintenance savings offsetting loan costs.
Advances city's zero emission vehicle roadmap and greenhouse gas reduction goals.

description: Multi-unit garbage program to shift to utility funding January 2028.
Property owners would pay utility fees based on bin size.
This replaces current funding through property taxes.

chips.text: Recommended
Staff explained two years of work needed for utility setup.
Apartments and condominiums in Saskatoon.

description: Recommends approving a Climate Action Strategy for Saskatoon.
It includes net zero and climate resilience playbooks.
Initiatives require future budget approval, not funded now.

chips.text: Recommended
Mayor Block noted the urban canopy unites the city and is a unique treasure.
Climate change increases home insurance rates and grocery prices for residents.
Saskatoon Climate Hub urged adequate funding; SOS Trees wants opt-out boulevard tree policy.
Strategy includes actions for Indigenous-led housing and low-income household support.
Saskatoon expects more hot days, wildfire smoke, and unpredictable rainfall/drought.

speakers.name: Caroline Dinter
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Climate Action Strategy
said: Supports the strategy, especially urban forest as a key part.
Recommends reinstating opt-out policy for boulevard tree planting.
Create incentives for private tree planting and conserve natural areas.

speakers.name: Carroll Chubb
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: The Climate Action Strategy
said: Urges council to adopt and adequately fund the Climate Action Strategy.
Strategy must be implemented urgently to meet net-zero goals.
Increase energy efficiency standards for buildings and create resilient infrastructure.

description: Saskatoon needs new biosolids pipelines; Martensville gets water/wastewater.
R.M. of Corman Park conditions threaten 2028 project completion.
Committee recommends negotiating reasonable agreement with R.M. and Martensville.

chips.text: Recommended
Administration states R.M. conditions exceed their own easement policies.
Martensville's growth is stalled without new wastewater infrastructure.
Administration believes R.M. lacks legal ability to impose certain conditions.

description: City utilities summarize 2025 operations and projects.
City fulfills public reporting on 2025 water works.

chips.text: Recommended
